value: mahogany plumage with darker lacing, resembling a wild pheasant, which gives the breed its name
thought to be a precursor of the Hamburg breed

meaty breast for a light breed, historically popular with farmers

history_summary.value: The Old English Pheasant Fowl is an old utility breed from rural Yorkshire and Lancashire, named for its pheasant-like plumage and formally named with a breed club in 1914. It is thought to be one of the ancestors of the Hamburg and remains rare today.
